He has completed his [[true freshman]] season as a [[forward (basketball)|forward]] for the [[2011–12 Baylor Bears basketball team|2011–12 team]]. He was born and raised in the [[Chicago metropolitan area]] until the age of 13, at which point, he moved to live with an uncle in North Carolina so that he could live a better life. He attended four different high schools, but eventually became one of the top ten high school basketball prospects in the class of 2011. He played for [[USA Basketball]] in the 2010 [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]]. Early in his senior year, he tore his [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) rendering him incapable of playing the remainder of the season. In his freshman season at [[Baylor University]], the team set school records for its best start (17–0), longest winning streak (17) and highest ranking (3/3). Following the [[2011–12 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season]], he was named the Big 12 co-Freshman of the Year and was recognized as an honorable mention All-Big 12 and a Big 12 All-Rookie Team selection by the Big 12 coaches. He was named Big 12 Freshman of the Year by ''[[Sporting News]]''. ==High school career== At age 13, his uncle Lamont Taylor from [[Fairmont, North Carolina]] took Miller in to get him away from the Chicago street life.{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/11/01-NC-Deuce-Bello-Quincy-Miller-november-mag.aspx|title=Deuce Bello, Quincy Miller join forces, form feared hardwood duo|accessdate=2011-12-29|date=2010-11-01|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=Parker, Brandon}} He transferred from [[North Chicago High School]] and played his freshman season for [[Fairmont High School (North Carolina)|Fairmont High School]] before transferring to [[Quality Education Academy]] where he grew {{convert|8|in|cm|1}} as a sophomore. Miller was relatively unknown until the 2009 Pangos All-American Camp and the Hoop Jamboree. Miller had began playing AAU basketball for D-One Sports. Then by July 2009 he was a top 10 class of 2011 prospect by [[Scout.com]] and top 25 by ''[[PrepStar]]'' and had interest from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]], [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{cite web|url=http://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/2009-07-22-miller-gboa-challenge-of-champions_N.htm|title=Top recruit Miller gets a chance to play in front of top programs|accessdate=2011-12-30|date=2009-07-22|work=[[USA Today]]|author=Sun, Victoria}} Late in Miller's 2009–10 junior season, he began receiving significant support from the 2010 ''[[ESPN HS]]'' [[Mr. Basketball USA]] voters who moved him into 11th place.{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/03/05-tracker-NHSI-opens-up-scenarios.aspx|title=Tracker: NHSI opens up scenarios|accessdate=2011-12-29|date=2010-03-05|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=Flores, Ronnie}}{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/03/12-tracker-sullinger.aspx|title=Tracker: History in the making |accessdate=2011-12-29|date=2010-03-13|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=Flores, Ronnie}} At the time, he was competing for Quality Education Academy in [[Winston-Salem, NC|Winston-Salem]]. He led the school to the National Christian Schools Athletic Association title.{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/08/elite-24-roster-bios.aspx|title=2010 Elite 24 player bios |accessdate=2011-12-29|date=2010-08-05|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=}} Following the season he was named a second-team ESPNHIGHSCHOOL.com All-American forward and announced his transfer to [[Westchester Country Day School]] of [[High Point, NC|High Point]] where his close friend Deuce Bello played. At the time, he held offers from Duke and Kentucky.{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/04/26-Quick-Shots.aspx|title=Quick Shots: Quincy Miller on the move|accessdate=2011-12-29|date=2010-04-26|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=Jordan, Jason}} He announced that along with the transfer, he would be changing jersey numbers from 35 to 22. The following summer ''[[SLAM Magazine]]'' rated him as the top prospect in the class of 2011 before he appeared at the June 2010 Pangos All-American Camp.{{cite web|last= Bohn |first=Rodger|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2010/06/slam-fresh-50-2011/|title=SLAM Fresh 50 – 2011: A new No. 1? |publisher=[[SLAM Magazine]] |date=2010-06-02 |accessdate=2012-03-04}}{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/06/05-Pangos-day-one.aspx|title=Amir Garrett, Myck Kabongo kickstart Pangos camp|accessdate=2011-12-29|date=2010-06-05|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=Flores, Ronnie}} After leading his team in [[rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] in the camp's "Cream of the Crop" All-Star finale game,{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/06/07-Pangos-Stats-and-awards.aspx?pursuit=BoysBasketball|title=Pangos stats & awards|accessdate=2011-12-29|date=2010-06-08|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=Flores, Ronnie}} Miller earned team MVP honors.{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/06/07-Pangos-wrap.aspx|title=Pangos: Cream of the crop emerges|accessdate=2011-12-29|date=2010-06-08|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=Flores, Ronnie}} In June 2010, Miller was the [[sixth man]] for the gold medal-winning team at the [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]]. He led the team in rebounding average for the tournament, was second in scoring average, and made the game-winning [[three-point field goal|3-point]] shot with 25 seconds remaining in the championship The following week, he played at the [[UIC Pavilion]] in the fourth annual [[adidas]] Nations global experience with many of the world's elite high school players.{{cite web|url=http://dimemag.com/2010/08/tune-in-to-the-adidas-nations-championship-game-tonight/|title=Tune In To The Aditions Championship Game Tonight|accessdate=2012-01-04|date=2010-08-09|author=Phillips, Aron|work=[[Dime Magazine]]}} In the September 2010 ScoutsFocus Elite 80 All Star Game in [[Greensboro, North Carolina]], after fans heckled him that his team was trailing, he rattled off 18 consecutive points.{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/09/25-Elite-80-notebook.aspx|title=Quincy Miller steals show at Elite 80|accessdate=2011-12-29|date=2010-09-27|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=Jordan, Jason}} Following in the footsteps of basketball players like [[LeBron James]], [[Kevin Love]], [[Tyreke Evans]] and [[Harrison Barnes]], Miller was the 2010–11 high school diary keeper for ''SLAM Magazine''.{{cite web|last= |first= |url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2010/07/quincy-miller-diary-no-1/ |title=Quincy Miller: Diary No. 1 |publisher=[[SLAM Magazine|Slam Online]] |date=2010-07-15 |accessdate=2010-08-26}} Once Miller and Bello were united, they were described as arguably the best high school basketball tandem in the country. Entering his senior season, Miller was a first team All-Southeast Region team selection by ''ESPN HS''.{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/11/15-basketball-annual-Southeast-Region-Adonis-Thomas.aspx|title=Southeast Region Breakdown: Adonis Thomas calls Memphis pickup legendary|accessdate=2011-12-29|date=2010-11-13|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=}} At the time he was listed in third in the 2010-2011 Preseason ESPNHS Mr. Basketball USA voting (behind [[Austin Rivers]] and [[Michael Kidd-Gilchrist|Mike Gilchrist]]).{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/11/29-preseason-tracker.aspx|title=Austin Rivers leads pack in first Mr. Basketball USA Tracker of the season|accessdate=2011-12-29|date=2010-11-29|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=Flores, Ronnie}} The team was preseason #32 in the POWERADE FAB 50 ESPNHS Boys' basketball team rankings.{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/team-rankings/2010-2011/Week-1.aspx?|title=POWERADE FAB 50 ESPNHS team rankings (Week 1)|accessdate=2011-12-29|date=|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=}} In December 2010, Miller suffered a torn [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]], ending his senior season, and high school career.{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2010/12/quincy-miller-out-for-season/|title=Quincy Miller Out For Season|work=SLAMOnline.com|author=|date=December 20, 2010|accessdate=February 10, 2011}}{{cite web|url=http://rise.espn.go.com/boys-basketball/articles/2010/12/20-quick-shots.aspx|title=Oak Hill coach Steve Smith notches 800th win; Quincy Miller tears ACL|accessdate=2011-12-29|date=2010-12-20|work=[[ESPN HS]]|author=Flores, Ronnie}} As a senior, he was ineligible for the [[McDonald's All-American Game]], but was an honorary All-American selection for the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] game.
